name: Question 13
problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion with damping. The position of the particle $y(t)$ at time $t$ is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+5y=25t.
$$

Which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for $y(t)?$

I. $y=R{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+ϕ)+5t-2$

II. $y=R{e}^{-2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+ϕ)+5t-2$

III. $y={e}^{-t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)+t-5$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
worked_solution:
The general solution is the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution:

$$
y(t)={y}_{c}(t)+{y}_{p}(t)
$$

First, we find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(t),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation ${y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+5y=0.$ Writing down and solving the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +5 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +1)-1+5 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2}+4 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2} & =-4 \\ \lambda +1 & =\pm 2\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-1\pm 2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(t)$ can be expressed in any of the following forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{c}(t) & ={e}^{-t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡2t), \\ {y}_{c}(t) & =R{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+ϕ), \\ {y}_{c}(t) & =R{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+ϕ).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(t).$ Since the external force is a linear function, we assume that the particular solution is also a linear function,

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\alpha t+\beta .
$$

By substituting the particular solution into the differential equation and equating coefficients, we find that $\alpha =5$ and $\beta =-2.$ So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=5t-2.
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & ={e}^{-t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)+5t-2, \\ y(t) & =R{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+ϕ)+5t-2, \\ y(t) & =R{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+ϕ)+5t-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Only I matches the forms above. Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

Question 13

A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion with damping. The position of the particle y(t) at time t is governed by the equation

y″+2y′+5y=25t.

Which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for y(t)?

  1. y=Re−tcos⁡(2t+ϕ)+5t−2
  2. y=Re−2tsin⁡(t+ϕ)+5t−2
  3. y=e−t(Acos⁡2t+Bsin⁡2t)+t−5
Note that A, B, R and ϕ are constants.

a
I and II only
b
II only
c
I and III only
d
III only
e
I only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The general solution is the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution:

y(t)=yc(t)+yp(t)

First, we find the complementary solution yc(t), which is the solution to the homogeneous equation y″+2y′+5y=0. Writing down and solving the characteristic equation gives

λ2+2λ+5=0(λ2+2λ+1)−1+5=0(λ+1)2+4=0(λ+1)2=−4λ+1=±2iλ=−1±2i.

Therefore the complimentary function yc(t) can be expressed in any of the following forms:

yc(t)=e−t(Acos⁡2t+Bsin⁡2t),yc(t)=Re−tcos⁡(2t+ϕ),yc(t)=Re−tsin⁡(2t+ϕ).

Next, we find the particular solution yp(t). Since the external force is a linear function, we assume that the particular solution is also a linear function,

yp(t)=αt+β.

By substituting the particular solution into the differential equation and equating coefficients, we find that α=5 and β=−2. So, the particular solution is

yp(t)=5t−2.

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

y(t)=e−t(Acos⁡2t+Bsin⁡2t)+5t−2,y(t)=Re−tcos⁡(2t+ϕ)+5t−2,y(t)=Re−tsin⁡(2t+ϕ)+5t−2.

Only I matches the forms above. Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
